proposal: The Mandate recommends linking pay and awards to performance (merit pay) and moving federal pay and benefits toward a market model with OPM overseeing pay-setting for high-demand occupations, and suggests further steps might be considered to bring federal retirement benefits closer to private-sector plans. It says most of this requires legislation and that, in the meantime, political executives should use existing pay and awards strategically to reward good performance.

status_summary: The administrative piece the Mandate says is possible without Congress is operating: OPM guidance of 2025-08-11 told agencies to direct larger awards to top performers, and OPM's 2026-09-21 memo steers at least 60 percent of FY2026 bonus pools for career SES, SP and GS employees to those rated Level 4 or 5 and limits combined Level 4 and 5 ratings to 40 percent of covered employees, with waivers of up to 10 percentage points available on request. On pay, the 2026 General Schedule raise was 1.0 percent with locality rates unchanged (OPM memo of 2025-12-18), EO 14368 asked OPM to assess up to 3.8 percent for some law enforcement staff, and the President's alternative pay plan for 2027 (letter dated 2026-08-26, House Document 119-189) sets the General Schedule and locality adjustments at zero and, separately, directs OPM to raise 2027 compensation for law enforcement personnel by 3.8 percent. OPM's critical position pay final rule (2026-08-26) moves approval of the highest rates from the President to the OPM Director, a limited step toward OPM oversight of pay for hard-to-fill roles. The Mandate's statutory pieces were not enacted: the House reconciliation bill's federal retirement changes were removed in the Senate in June 2025 and, per a FEDweek analysis, the high-5, higher-contribution and supplement changes were not in the law signed 2025-07-04 (Public Law 119-21), whose table of contents lists no provision amending federal retirement or pay. OPM's FEHB request for information (2026-09-15) raises possible premium caps but proposes no change in the government share.

timeline.event: The reconciliation law is signed as Public Law 119-21. Its table of contents lists no provision amending FERS or CSRS retirement benefits, employee contributions or federal pay; the one federal-benefits entry is Sec. 90101 (FEHB improvements), whose text was not read. A FEDweek analysis of 2025-07-23 reports that the law kept the high-3 formula and the FERS supplement and omitted higher FERS contributions, and the Senate version released 2025-06-29 had already dropped the House bill's federal benefit changes.

OPM issues government-wide guidance directing larger performance awards toward top performers: strengthen performance management, normalize ratings, reserve the largest awards for exceptional contributions, and use more non-cash awards such as time off and quality step increases.

EO 14368 sets 2026 pay schedules and asks OPM to assess up to a total 3.8 percent increase for certain civilian law enforcement staff; an OPM memo of the same date states a 1.0 percent across-the-board increase with locality rates unchanged, effective 2026-01-11.

OPM final rule on critical position pay (effective the same day): Executive Schedule Level I becomes the default ceiling, above-EX-I rates need OPM Director approval rather than presidential approval, and affected employees cannot grieve or appeal reductions. Statutory 800-position cap unchanged.

The President transmits to the Speaker of the House an Alternative Plan for Pay Adjustments for 2027 (House Document 119-189, under 5 U.S.C. 5304a) that sets General Schedule and locality pay adjustments at zero, and separately directs OPM to raise 2027 compensation for law enforcement personnel by 3.8 percent. The document was referred to the House Oversight and Armed Services Committees on 2026-08-27; Government Executive reported it on 2026-08-28.
OPM publishes a request for information (comments due 2026-11-16) on FEHB and PSHB plan options, including whether to cap plan premiums; it proposes no change to premium sharing.

OPM FY2026 awards guidance: at least 60 percent of career SES, SP and GS bonus pools to Level 4 and 5 performers, combined Level 4 and 5 ratings capped at 40 percent (waivers of up to 10 points), smaller Level 3 awards, a separate bonus pool for Schedule Policy/Career employees, and suggested pay-adjustment ranges for career SES.

title: Tie pay and awards to performance; move pay and benefits toward private-sector norms
uncertainties: The enacted-law finding on retirement rests on the table of contents of Public Law 119-21 (govinfo) plus a FEDweek planner's column (2025-07-23) and a Government Executive report of the Senate text (2025-06-29); the full body of the law was not searched (the text of Sec. 90101, FEHB improvements, was not located), so a retirement or pay provision outside the table of contents is not ruled out. The EO 14368 text did not show the General Schedule percentage (schedules are images), so the 1.0 percent figure comes from OPM's memo. The OPM 2026-09-21 memo was re-read on opm.gov in the 2026-10-16 review; the 2025-12-18 pay memo, the FEHB request for information and the press and column sources were not re-verified then. Not checked: FY2027 budget proposals on FERS or any 2026 bill touching retirement, merit pay or locality pay; a search for such bills was not run. OPM's May 2026 proposal to eliminate time-in-grade and its 2026 appraisal rules (tracked in c03-03) are not pay-setting changes and are not counted here.
